summary:
We are developing software for the spacecraft that collects data on vital signs measured by sensors in the devices worn by the astronaut.
If any anomaly in the vital signs is detected, the astronaut—by means of LED indicators— as well as the spacecraft and the Deep Space Network on Earth, will be alerted so that appropriate measures can be taken.
Our project addresses this challenge by providing a way to monitor health using sensors that immediately alert astronauts to any anomalies before major problems arise; its significance lies in the fact that astronauts can take immediate action, as data is generated every few seconds.
details:
It works as follows: sensors generate data on the astronauts' vital signs, and software collects this information via Bluetooth, processes it, and displays it on a panel that summarizes each astronaut's health status. If an anomaly is detected, an alert is triggered—using lights to indicate the severity level—signaling the astronauts to return to the spacecraft, which allows for rapid intervention to prevent more serious issues.
The impact of our project is that astronauts are kept informed about their own health and that of their crewmates during missions whether inside or outside the spacecraft, enabling them to take action quickly.
Tools used to develop the project:
- Languages: HTML, CSS, JavaScript y Python

- Libraries: Three.Js, GSAP scrollTrigger

- Software: Claude code, Visual Studio Code and Netlify
- Hardware: Nórdic nRF2840, ESP 32 mini, ET2016C-R, PPG Sensor (max30102), Glass-encapsulated NTC thermistor, accelerometer (LIS3DH), ECG Sensor (AD8232)
